nodes.description: A single substitution at the catalytic cysteine that abolishes phosphatase activity while leaving the protein's fold and its hair cell localisation intact. Homozygotes are severely to profoundly deaf, have the same stereocilia fusion and hair cell degeneration as the null alleles, and males are infertile. It is the experiment that ties both phenotypes to the enzyme activity itself.

The standard intervention for severe-to-profound sensorineural loss. The lesion in mice is in the hair cells, which an implant bypasses, but the mismatch between surviving hair cells and profound deafness in Cdc14a mice raises the possibility of a defect elsewhere in the auditory pathway, and the mouse Cdc14a reporter is also active in spiral ganglion, which an implant relies on.

The presentation in the founding Tunisian family, in the Iranian family of the 2016 gene report, and in the two families of the 2020 functional study: deafness present from birth, severe to profound. In other families the loss was first noticed between ages 1 and 3, or at school entry, so congenital onset is common but not universal. No newborn hearing screen result has been reported for any affected child.

nodes.description: CDC14A is a dual-specificity phosphatase whose catalytic domain (DSPc, residues 217-325) dephosphorylates serine, threonine and tyrosine residues. The HIIMS alleles remove this activity: the missense substitutions p.Arg312Gln and p.Arg312Gly are predicted to destabilise the substrate-binding acidic groove, p.Gln320Pro to prevent activation of the catalytic water molecule, and the N-terminal truncations and exon 10 splice variant delete the domain altogether. The decisive test was made in mouse: a single cysteine-to-serine change at the catalytic residue (p.Cys278Ser), which kills activity without altering the protein's fold or its localisation in hair cells, reproduces deafness and male infertility as completely as the knockout alleles. Phosphatase activity is therefore required for both organs, which is the reason this node sits upstream of both the cochlear and the testicular lesion.

nodes.description: The nonsyndromic DFNB32 alleles truncate CDC14A after the two globular domains. The 623-residue protein ends in a 278-residue intrinsically disordered region (IDR) that carries the nuclear export signal. Exon 11 truncations would be expected to trigger nonsense-mediated decay of the full-length transcript, but exon 11 is the final exon of a shorter isoform, and the p.Arg345Ter transcript is present at normal levels in patient leukocytes. The resulting protein (residues 1-345) was purified, crystallised and shown to keep its fold and its phosphatase activity. What it loses is the tail, and with it, nuclear export. The node therefore describes a protein that is catalytically competent but in the wrong place, which is what separates this subtype from HIIMS.

nodes.description: Full-length CDC14A in inner ear hair cells is cytoplasmic and concentrated in the hair bundle and along the kinocilium, with no detectable nuclear signal. nodes.description: In Cdc14a mutant mice the organ of Corti is built normally. Stereocilia bundles and kinocilia look normal at postnatal days 7 to 9, so CDC14A is not needed to make a hair bundle. After the onset of hearing, stereocilia fuse, inner hair cells degenerate ahead of outer hair cells, and by postnatal day 90 about half of the hair cells in the apical turn are gone. Outer hair cell function is lost early: distortion-product otoacoustic emissions are absent from postnatal day 16. The stria vascularis is not involved, since the endocochlear potential is normal. One result does not fit a pure hair-cell-loss account. Mice are profoundly deaf at postnatal day 90 while about half their hair cells remain, which the authors read as a second, unidentified defect in the auditory pathway.

nodes.description: In infertile Cdc14a mutant male mice, seminiferous tubules degenerate, with loss of spermatogenic cells, vacuolisation of Sertoli cells, spermatid heads retained at the basement membrane and spermatids clumped around residual bodies. Epididymal sperm counts fall and the remaining sperm are often abnormal. A second, independent knockout line describes the same subfertility and adds a meiotic phenotype, with an excess of pachytene spermatocytes and raised levels of the CDC14A substrates CDC25A, WEE1 and PR-SET7 in the testis. This is the HIIMS-specific limb of the pathograph; males carrying DFNB32-type alleles do not show it, and females have no counterpart.
